title: Color-Vision Deficiency Compensation: Reading Standard Vertical & Horizontal Signal Positions

no_head_on_same_lane.note: All vehicles in foreground/background face same direction away from viewer; no opposing head-on pair in same lane.

no_rhd_cabin.note: Only exterior rear views of cars shown; no interiors or steering wheels visible to judge.

single_bulb_signal.note: Both signals show three lit lenses at once: left vertical has red+amber+green all bright, right horizontal has red+amber+green all bright, violates at most one lit.

us_right_hand_traffic.note: Cars drive forward on right side with yellow dashed line on LEFT of travel lane and white lane markings on RIGHT, consistent with US right-hand traffic.

zero_text.note: No letters, numbers, or words visible anywhere; signals, road, cars and sky are blank shapes.

scene_match.note: Shows left vertical housing and right horizontal housing against sky with correct red-yellow-green order, matching described diagram.

result.summary: Position order is correct but both signals show all three lenses lit simultaneously, failing single-bulb rule, requiring rejection.

teaching_correct.note: Vertical top-to-bottom red-yellow-green and horizontal left-to-right red-yellow-green order is standard and correct for color-vision position learning.

result.what_i_see: A large vertical traffic signal in left foreground and a horizontal signal on the right span a multi-lane road with several cars seen from behind driving away under a sunset sky.
